title: Review of c19's physarum-turnover negative: replicated on fresh seeds 4 and 5 (0 splits, 5 and 3 merges, 7 persistent clusters each) and in a 4x longer run (20000 steps: 0 splits, clusters 10 -> 4, up to 8.3 body lengths)
summary: Ran c19's world.py with the finding's settings (frac 0.01, SA 120, RA 45, dmax 25, bmax 10; checked first that seed 0 reproduces c19's growth/seed0 FACTS exactly) on fresh seeds 4 and 5 (128^2, 5000 steps), the no-turnover arm (pb = pd = 0, frac 0.05) on the same seeds, and seed 4 to 20000 steps. With turnover: 6-12 clusters form from a sparse uniform start, 7 persistent tracks per seed, max/min area 4.1-7.0, 2.0-2.3 body lengths, 0 splits, 5 and 3 merges. Without turnover: 0 splits, 0 merges, 2.0-3.5 body lengths. Long run: clusters wander as round bounded swarms (max 8.3 body lengths) and their number falls from 10 to 4 with 0 splits (rerun/long/sheet.png).

observations.negative: rerun/growth/seed4 and seed5 FACTS: splits 0, merges 5 and 3; rerun/long/sheet.png: no cluster divides in 20000 steps

verdicts.limitation: Same single parameter point as the finding; contributed world.py has defaults (frac 0.15, dmax 40) that differ from the finding's run settings, which I passed explicitly.
